rationale: The definitions agree: additive category, all kernels and cokernels, and every canonical coimage-to-image map is an isomorphism.

The source index term points to the class-based criterion of Lemma 3.3.1. The tagged Stacks lemma supplies the analogous acyclic-resolution mechanism, but this term is only a cross-sectional concept, not a standalone assertion.
Grothendieck's additive category is the Stacks preadditive category with zero object and binary biproducts; Stacks packages this as finite products.

The derived category term is fully represented by the Stacks category definition together with the source-specific convention-boundary remark; the admitted p. 122 body coordinate supplies the exact source content and no additional live statement is needed.
Both treatments form Čech cohomology from coverings and refinement maps; the tagged Stacks section is the direct modern home for the indexed notion.
The source term names the package developed in Section 3.5. Stacks has the corresponding canonical exact sequence, but the index headword itself carries no separate theorem to identify.
Stacks now defines a cogenerator by the exact dual factorization criterion: every proper quotient is detected by a map to the cogenerator which does not factor through that quotient.
The source headword indexes the later cohomological-dimension discussion. The tagged Stacks proposition is a directly related spectral bound, not a literal definition of the term.

Stacks now defines a family of supports, Gamma_Phi, and H^p_Phi as its universal right-derived cohomological functor, including negative and zero degrees and acyclic-resolution computation. This is the exact source notion, not only the closed-subset special case.

The source uses method of coverings as an umbrella for several Čech constructions and acyclicity criteria. The two tagged sections provide the infrastructure, but no single labelled statement is the term.
Stacks uses delta-functor for an exact cohomological sequence in degrees n>=0 between abelian categories; Tohoku's term points to broader nonexact partial-degree data with merely additive codomain.
No local generic lowering-degree delta-star notion exists. The nearby exact-duality lemma changes variance but does not define delta-star, and its TeX label has no tag entry.

The printed contents says derived delta-functor while the printed body heading and definition say universal delta-functor; direct-source replay establishes a genuine title variant, so this contents term is retained only as a structural alias and is not mapped to a Stacks tag.
The local definitions give derived functors and their cohomology-object functors; Tohoku's body uses the classical injective/projective-resolution realization.

Stacks now constructs the category of representations of a directed graph with integral path relations as additive functors from the corresponding free preadditive path category modulo relations. This is the source's category of diagrams in a Stacks-native formulation.
Stacks now defines a directed graph scheme by a vertex set, arrow set, and source and target maps, then uses it to construct graph-shaped and additive diagrams with relations.
The object map, morphism maps, identity preservation, and composition preservation agree exactly for covariant functors.

Stacks now states the generator criterion as the singleton case of a set-indexed family of generators, matching the source's factorization-through-proper-subobjects definition in the abelian setting used by this chapter.

The source global Hom is obtained from morphisms or global sections of the internal Hom sheaf; the tagged Stacks lemma gives the same Hom identification.
This is only the chapter-level subject heading, not a mathematical assertion with a single local Stacks target.
The source inductive system is the Stacks system over a preorder and its inductive limit is precisely the colimit universal property.
Both define an arbitrary set-indexed product by the same universal property and canonical projections.
The source's arbitrary direct sum in a category is the Stacks coproduct, with the same universal property and canonical injections/coprojections.
Stacks gives the extension definition and proves its equivalence with exactness of Hom(-,I), exactly the two source formulations.
The source and Stacks use the same Leray spectral sequence for a continuous map and a sheaf, with the tagged lemma giving the actual spectral sequence.
The source term indexes two passage-to-the-limit results rather than defining one object. The tagged Stacks section is the verified thematic counterpart.
The source local Ext is the sheaf-valued derived Hom construction. The tagged Stacks Ext section develops that same local derived object.
The introduction expressly records multiplicative structures as an omitted topic. It is therefore a structural index concept, and no source-backed labelled target should be asserted.

Stacks now proves pointwise permanence of additive and abelian structure, kernels, cokernels, images, coimages, exactness, products, coproducts, AB3 through AB6, and all dual AB3* through AB6* conditions for additive diagram categories.
The source projective system is the inverse system over a preorder and its projective limit is the Stacks limit universal property.
Stacks gives the lifting definition and its equivalent exactness-of-Hom characterization, matching the dual source notion.
Stacks constructs the same abelian Serre quotient and adds its universal property; Grothendieck's 'thick' subcategory is Stacks' Serre subcategory.
Stacks' resolution functor resolves complexes into injective complexes and is not Tohoku's exact functor from objects to complexes computing a fixed F.
The source and Stacks impose the same local gluing and uniqueness conditions on sections over an open cover.
The source Ext sheaves of modules are the sheaf-valued right-derived Hom objects developed in the tagged Stacks section.
The source sheaf Hom assigns local module morphisms and sheafifies them; the tagged Stacks section develops the same internal Hom sheaf.
No local definition of an additive functor into a category of spectral sequences was found; Stacks develops functorial spectral sequences without this packaged term.
Stacks separates page data, bigraded shifts, and convergence; Tohoku bundles bigrading, eventual stability, filtered abutment, and E-infinity identifications into one notion.
This is the organizing topic for the source's specialized nonabelian obstruction argument, not a single definition, and no directly matching tagged Stacks statement was verified.
The two actions of P on F and F-prime are proof data internal to Proposition 3.4.2. They should remain a structural step without an invented external match.
The source only notes an analogy with abstract algebraic geometry and adds characteristic and fixed-point qualifications; it does not state a theorem with an exact labelled Stacks target.

Stacks verifies the affine basis, affine intersections for separated schemes, affine vanishing for every quasi-coherent module, and the resulting Cech comparison; these statements cover the coherent classical-variety application in greater generality.

This is Cartan's coordinate-cube application of the source's special-cover criterion; no labelled Stacks result states this hyperplane-cover reduction.
The finite-group algebraic-variety case is an application; Stacks has the cited finite-fibre vanishing result but not this equivariant computation as a matching theorem.

Stacks now records the source's fixed-point-free specialization: trivial stabilizers force all positive higher invariant direct images to vanish and canonically identify equivariant cohomology with quotient-space cohomology; the earlier descent lemma also supplies the stated a priori equivalence of sheaf categories.
This first half only announces an application of the preceding supported Leray result and contains no independent mathematical assertion.
This continuation merely identifies algebraic varieties with their Zariski topology as the announced setting; it gives no standalone comparison theorem.
This only advertises an application to modular-group cohomology and cites external computations; it is not a local theorem to map.
The naturality square for connecting maps is the second Stacks axiom; the surrounding Stacks definition additionally assumes nonnegative degrees, abelian codomain, and exactness.
This introduces the long sequence whose consecutive composites must vanish; Stacks requires that same sequence to be exact, hence supplies a stronger packaged axiom.
Tohoku only requires the displayed sequence to be a complex. Stacks' delta-functor definition requires exactness and therefore implies, but is not equivalent to, this axiom.

Stacks now proves the source's bijection on nonabelian H1 as a bijection between isomorphism classes of torsors. For A=Π(F), B=Π(G), C=Π(H), and P=AG, it identifies P=B×_C H and B→C as sectionwise surjective, proves every H-torsor lifts to a P-torsor, and proves uniqueness using the flasque twisted kernel A^E≅Π(F^E). It explicitly avoids the false general claim that flasqueness is local and asserts uniqueness only up to isomorphism.
This unit is the cocycle-level surjectivity argument supporting the preceding bijection, rather than an independently reusable theorem.

Stacks now formalizes the source's specific pointwise-envelope quotient: for an abelian normal sheaf F⊂G it defines A=Π(F), B=Π(G), P=AG as the local-product subsheaf, and F'=A/F as the quotient sheaf; proves A∩G=F and the conjugation action; and constructs the sheaf-of-sets epimorphism u(ag)=a mod F with neutral fibre G, crossed identity, and right-G coset fibres. It explicitly does not claim sectionwise surjectivity or that u is a group homomorphism.
The claim computes the derived H2 of the specially constructed complement-constant sheaf; the actual Stacks TeX contains no version of this counterexample.

Stacks now states and proves the source's finite closed-cover star construction: it defines E_x(R) and O_x(R), proves x lies in O_x(R) contained in E_x(R) and E_y(R) is contained in E_x(R) whenever y lies in O_x(R), and proves O_x(R) is an open neighbourhood because the excluded cover members form a finite union of closed subsets.

The new lemma proves coherence of the middle term, Yoneda classification and Baer addition in the analytic equivariant category, and the natural complex vector space structure, exactly closing the source claim.

The new lemma proves that the equivariant holomorphic bundle-module equivalence identifies fixed-endpoint bundle extensions with Yoneda Ext^1, preserves Baer sum, and then applies the locally-free edge isomorphism and evaluation to obtain exactly H^1(X;G,O(E^dual tensor F)).

Stacks directly proves global Cech H1 equals derived H1 on every space and, in the tagged section containing the paracompact comparison, equality in all degrees on paracompact spaces; this gives both source cases without its delta-functor premise.
Both statements identify first Čech cohomology with derived-functor H1 for abelian sheaves; the tagged Stacks lemma states the comparison directly.

Stacks now proves for every n at a fixed orbit point that the stalk of the derived abelian-sheaf-valued equivariant Hom functor is canonically Ext over the skew stabilizer ring, under local finite-presentation, local left-coherence, and pointwise left-Noetherian hypotheses. This pointwise theorem covers the source's coherent and Noetherian setting without claiming a noncommutative module structure on internal Hom, a right-sided variant, or any comparison outside the stated hypotheses.

The same theorem proves injectivity of equivariant-injective stalks under a local left-coherence image condition and left Noetherianity of the single stalk. The comparison is only asserted as an isomorphism of abelian groups, and no module structure on noncommutative internal Hom, right-module analogue, averaging argument, or unrestricted preservation of injectives by stalks is claimed.

Because the pointwise-envelope quotient makes u an epimorphism and F' abelian, the class is neutral exactly when Q reduces to a G-torsor, equivalently when [Q] lies in the image of G-torsor classes. No degree-two sign is asserted at this stage.

It does not repeat the false generator assertion for arbitrary diagram schemes.

Stacks now constructs the direct image of a G-sheaf along a G-equivariant continuous map, including its sectionwise G-action and all supported algebraic-structure variants; the quotient-map case is the stated trivial-action specialization.

The new bounded lemma gives the p.160 quotient-as-locally-principal-germs statement and, under factorial local rings, its identification with the Weil-divisor sheaf. It reuses the already proved locally-UFD exact sequence and does not conflate the p.161 cohomology successor or the analytic lifting boundary.

Consequently H^1 of the unit sheaf is the Weil divisor class group and all higher cohomology vanishes. No projective-bundle lifting assertion is included.

This remains a structural interpretation of the displayed edge maps.

Stacks now constructs canonical functorial transition maps for every ordinary refinement of open G-coverings, proves choice independence and transitivity, and proves agreement with the usual map whenever an equivariant refinement function is given; its two-sided free-replacement roof corrects the source's stabilizer obstruction.

Its derived colimit comparison is asserted only under the separately stated Gamma_X^G-acyclicity condition for extension by zero, and its ordinary supported-cohomology comparison additionally assumes that Phi is paracompactifying; neither extra condition is inferred from the neighbourhood hypothesis.

Stacks now proves that the finite-generator subsheaves form a filtered system with colimit F, that the chosen Serre subcategory is closed under filtered colimits by the direct-sum-and-cokernel presentation, and hence reduces the argument exactly to finitely generated sheaves.

Stacks now constructs the two canonical kernel-to-cokernel morphisms for two five-term exact sequences with a common middle object, canonically identifies the two cross-kernels, and proves both resulting exact sequences (5.2.12).

Stacks gives a strengthened corrected construction: it forms the free-indexed replacement G times I, proves that its equivariant refinement map is a quasi-isomorphism, and free-replaces both coverings so an equivariant comparison always exists; this repairs the invalid one-sided step in the printed source and proves free coverings cofinal.

Stacks now constructs, functorially for every sheaf of sets, the pointwise product sheaf U↦∏_{x∈U}F_x and its canonical germ monomorphism. For sheaves of possibly noncommutative groups this is a flasque group sheaf (and remains abelian in the abelian case), with surjectivity obtained by identity fillers.
